title: What Newborn Sleep Really Looks Like
hook: Newborns sleep a lot — but in short bursts, with no day-night rhythm yet. Frequent night waking to feed is normal and expected, not a problem to fix.
key_points: Newborns sleep many hours a day, but only in short stretches of an hour or two at a time.
There's no day-night rhythm at first — regular sleep cycles don't develop until around 6 months.
Waking often through the night to feed is normal and expected for a newborn.
Don't expect a schedule yet — and back-sleeping on a firm, flat, bare surface still applies for every sleep.
content_html: If newborn sleep feels chaotic, that's because it is — by design. The AAP notes that newborns sleep a great deal across the day, on the order of 16 to 17 hours, but only in short stretches of an hour or two at a time. They don't yet have a day-night rhythm, and regular sleep cycles generally don't develop until around six months of age.
extra_html: That means frequent waking through the night to feed is normal and expected, not a sign anything is wrong, and there's no real schedule to enforce this early. What doesn't change is safe sleep: every nap and every night, place your baby on their back on a firm, flat, bare surface. The irregularity passes on its own as your baby matures. This is general guidance; if you're worried about your baby's sleep, feeding, or breathing, talk to your pediatrician.

related.title: A Safe Sleep Space for Baby
related.hook: Pediatric guidance for safer infant sleep is simple: a firm, flat surface with nothing in it — no pillows, blankets, bumpers, or soft toys.

related.title: Soothing a Fussy Newborn
related.hook: Newborns are wired to be calmed by sensations that echo the womb — holding, swaddling, gentle motion, white noise, and sucking. One rule overrides all: never, ever shake a baby.

flashcards.prompt: How do newborns typically sleep across the day?

choices.text: Many total hours, but in short stretches of an hour or two
One long block at night, awake all day
On a strict 4-hour schedule from birth

flashcards.explanation_html: The AAP notes newborns sleep about 16 to 17 hours a day but only 1 to 2 hours at a time, with no regular sleep cycles until around 6 months.

flashcards.prompt: Is waking up through the night to feed a problem in a newborn?
flashcards.back_html: No — it's normal and expected. Newborns have no day-night rhythm yet and wake frequently to feed. Regular sleep cycles develop around 6 months.

flashcards.prompt: Do safe-sleep rules change because newborn sleep is so irregular?

choices.text: No — back-sleeping on a firm, flat, bare surface applies for every sleep
Yes — anything goes as long as baby sleeps
Only for night sleep, not naps

flashcards.explanation_html: Irregular newborn sleep is normal, but safe-sleep basics — back-sleeping on a firm, flat, bare surface for every sleep — still apply.
